reviewer: adversarial finder (score not authoritative; see PROMPT-STANDARD "How to review a prompt")

gaps.property: Rule 4 (acceptance criteria must be observable) / property 2 (falsifiable) — the item is probably not achievable through the dependency API at all
gaps.problem: Item 7 is a blocker requiring a ramp crossing the highway with Δy >= 5.5 m between centrelines, verified with world.roads.sample. roads offers no lever for this. addNode(x,z) sets designY from terrain (network.js:41) and nothing may set it afterwards; opts.elevation is accepted at network.js:53 and then unconditionally overwritten in build.js:499 (`e.elevation = e.bridge ? 1 : 0`); nodeHeights() (build.js:470-481) derives every node y from the terrain-smoothed arm profiles; a deck appears only over water or where a blended profile happens to sit BRIDGE_MIN = 6 m above terrain. democity may not edit roads and section 7 tells it not to call terrain.modify. So the only route to 5.5 m of separation is terrain luck that must also hold at --seed 7 (item 21 re-grades item 7 there). A builder will burn a round discovering this, and the critic then caps the score at 6 for something the builder could not build.
gaps.fix: Name the mechanism or defer the clause. Add to item 7: 'roads derives node heights from terrain and ignores opts.elevation except for bridges (build.js:499); there is no public way to raise a ramp. Round 1: file docs/core-requests/democity.md asking roads for addNode(x,z,{designY}) or roads.setNodeHeight(id,y), and until it lands satisfy grade separation by carrying the ramp over the river or a mapped gully. Until the core request lands the Δy >= 5.5 m clause is ungraded (missing capability), not failed; the rest of item 7 — continuity, curvature <= 0.9 deg/m, >= 3 ramp/merge edges, median/barriers — grades as written.'

gaps.property: Rule 4 + property 2/3, and the standard's 'conflict with another module's ownership' — items 10, 12 and the section 8 contents contradict item 15
gaps.problem: props is real (the spec says so in section 7 and I confirmed it), and item 15 makes that absolute: 'with props real, stats().own.trees === 0 && own.lamps === 0'. But item 12 (major) requires a park with '>= 120 trees of >= 3 species by silhouette and >= 4 crown-colour variants ... and lamps', item 10 (major) requires 'street trees along >= 70 % of suburban frontage at 14-24 m spacing', item 12 requires a treed edge wrapping the built area, and section 8 repeats all of it as required contents. Every one of those objects belongs to props, whose place.js scatters forest from a slope/height/noise field 'outside roads and lots' and places lamps only along road edges — democity's only lever is where it puts roads and lots, which the spec never says. Worse, no item says where the tree count is read from: stats().own.trees is required to be 0, and world.props.items is only mentioned in item 15's proximity check. So the critic counts 120 trees by eye and the builder has no way to hit 4 crown colours. Three majors failing caps the score at 7.5.
gaps.fix: State the coupling and move the measurement: 'Park trees, the treed edge and suburban street trees come from props (place.js: forest scatters where there is no road and no lot; lamps and street furniture follow road edges). democity's lever is layout — leave the park polygon unlotted and unroaded so forest scatters into it, and run an alley or gravel path through it so props lamps it. Item 12's counts are probed from world.props.items filtered to the park polygon at capture time (kind, heading, scale are on each entry), never from stats().own.trees; species = distinct kind values, crown-colour variants = distinct (kind, scale bucket) pairs. If props' scatter yields < 120 in the park, that is inherited against props with the probe number as evidence, not democity's failure.' Alternatively carve an explicit exception in item 15 letting democity place ornament inside its own park/plaza polygons with props real, and give it a numeric cap.

gaps.property: Rule 7 (dependencies and their real APIs — 'the exact functions, so nothing is invented')
gaps.problem: Section 7 heads one merged list '`world.zones` / `ctx.modules.zoning`: paint · erase · bulk(fn) · lotsFor · freeLots · lotAt · cellAt · zonableAt · refresh · setOverlayVisible · stats · debugEdge'. Only paint, erase, lotsFor, freeLots, cellAt, lotAt, zonableAt and maxDepth are installed on world.zones (zoning/grid.js:460-467); bulk, refresh, setOverlayVisible, stats and debugEdge exist only on ctx.modules.zoning. Every other dependency in section 7 splits the two objects (world.roads vs ctx.modules.roads), so the merged form reads as 'either object works'. A builder who writes world.zones.bulk(fn) — the one call the spec insists on, because painting 11 000 cells singly blows the budget — throws inside showcase.setup, and section 8's own catch-all wrapper converts that into 'status ready, honest zero counts', i.e. a silently empty city. The same slip appears in step 11, which says to call `world.services.place(kind,…)` although item 15 gates on ctx.modules.services.place and section 7 warns that world.services.place is the core placeholder returning null.
gaps.fix: Split the zoning entry the way roads is split: '`world.zones`: paint · erase · lotsFor · freeLots · lotAt · cellAt · zonableAt · maxDepth · cells · lots · version (zoning/grid.js:460-467). `ctx.modules.zoning`: paint · erase · bulk(fn) · lotsFor · freeLots · lotAt · cellAt · zonableAt · refresh · setOverlayVisible · overlayVisible · stats · debugEdge · serialize/deserialize — bulk, refresh, setOverlayVisible and stats exist ONLY here.' And change step 11 to `ctx.modules.services.place(kind,…)`, matching item 15's gate.

gaps.property: Rule 7 + property 3 — a stated fact about the codebase that is false, and a budget rationale that rests on it
gaps.problem: Section 7 asserts 'traffic, services, transit, infoviews and tools are stubs — dependencies: [], api either {} or {serialize, deserialize}, showcase.setup a no-op', and item 15 repeats 'the stub's api is {}' for traffic. traffic is a complete module: src/modules/traffic/index.js imports LaneGraph and Traffic, and its api exposes spawnVehicle(kind, route), despawn(id), flowGrid() with A* routing, IDM car-following, signal phases and pedestrians. The consequence is not cosmetic: section 5's justification for the 220-draw-call declared budget is that it 'draws against the props (400) and traffic (150) allotments that are unused while those modules are stubs' — but the same spec says props is real, and traffic is real too, so neither allotment is free and the stated rationale for exceeding constants.js's democity: 50 no longer holds. A builder following section 7 also builds a vehicle/parked-car fallback layer (item 15: own.vehicles >= 120, own.parked >= 200) that can never activate.
gaps.fix: Correct the status paragraph to 'services, transit, infoviews and tools are stubs; terrain, roads, zoning, buildings, props, traffic, simulation, environment, effects, ui and audio are real (traffic exposes spawnVehicle/despawn/flowGrid with pedestrians and outside connections)'. Then restate the section 5 assumption on the real state: 'with props and traffic real, the only fallbacks that can fire are services and transit, so the declared budget is {drawCalls: N, triangles: M} sized for 14 landmark meshes plus one bus line and its stops; stats().own.drawCalls <= 50 whenever services and transit are also real.' Keep item 15's traffic lane as a documented dormant branch, or delete the vehicle-fallback numbers.

gaps.property: Property 3 (numeric) / property 2 (falsifiable) — six items carry eyeball clauses in a spec that measures everything else
gaps.problem: Item 10: '>= 70 % of their lots show a driveway to the kerb, a boundary and a lawn distinct in tone from terrain grass' (no probe, no ΔL threshold for 'distinct in tone'), '>= 4 distinguishable house silhouettes and >= 5 roof colours in one frame' (counted by eye at 180 m). Item 11: 'blocks >= 1.6x the downtown block area' — 'block' is never defined and stats() reports no blocks; '>= 2 gantry cranes or an equivalent silhouette' is an open loophole. Item 12: species and crown-colour counts, as above. Item 3: 'lit sources present and distinguishable' and '>= 2 lit signs'. Item 2's night_street clause: 'a lit downtown canyon at 22:00, not a suburban street'. Item 16: '>= 5 distinguishable vehicle silhouettes'. Each is a round-costing argument in a checklist that otherwise leaves none, and three of them sit inside blockers.
gaps.fix: Give each a probe row in probe.json fed from plan()/stats() and world data rather than from the frame: extend the api with `stats().suburb:{lots, withDriveway, withBoundary, withLawn, roofColours, silhouettes}` and `stats().industry:{blocks, meanBlockArea, cranes, silos, stacks}` and define a block as 'a face of the road graph bounded by street/avenue/gravel edges, area from its polygon'. Define 'lawn distinct in tone' as mean |ΔL| >= 12 against the adjacent terrain-grass patch at full resolution. Replace item 2's night_street sentence with the numbers already available: '>= 12 buildings taller than 40 m within 120 m of [-40,0,60], and >= 40 BRIGHT CLUSTERS in the frame'. Replace 'or an equivalent silhouette' with a named alternative (>= 2 gantry cranes, or >= 4 stacked-container rows plus a wharf edge >= 120 m).

gaps.property: Rule 7 (exact functions) — an incomplete copied table
gaps.problem: Section 7's world.roads.types line lists exactly five types (alley, gravel, street, avenue, highway), and item 1 requires 'all five road types present'. roads defines six (network.js:5-12): ramp { width 10, lanes 1, speed 60, oneWay true }. Item 7 requires '>= 3 ramp/merge edges' and section 2's stats() carries a `ramps` count, so the builder must pass type 'ramp' to addEdge — a string the spec's own exhaustive API surface never shows. A builder told 'nothing is invented' will instead build ramps as one-way highway edges and lose the merge geometry (build.js:215-221 detects a ramp as oneWay + lanes 1) plus the gore hatching.
gaps.fix: Add ramp to the copied types line: '`types` = {alley w8 l1 s30, gravel w8 l2 s30, street w16 l2 s50, avenue w24 l4 s60, highway w32 l6 s100, ramp w10 l1 s60 oneWay (network.js:11)}' and note that roads recognises a merge only when the ramp arm is oneWay with lanes 1 and not a ring member (build.js:215). Reword item 1 to 'all five of the non-ramp types present'.

gaps.property: Property 3 (numeric) — an unquantified requirement inside a hard time budget
gaps.problem: Item 23 requires world.economy.population >= 8 000 and jobs >= 3 000, and step 14 says to reach it with simulation.step(n). n is never given, and simulation.step runs synchronous 4 Hz ticks over every building (economy.js iterates the per-building records, sampling four grids per building). With 1 200-2 400 buildings this is the one step in the pipeline whose cost is unbounded, and it sits inside item 24's 25 s stageMs ceiling and item 19's budget. Neither the tick count, a growth expectation, nor a fallback if 8 000 is not reached in the budget is stated.
gaps.fix: State the number and the escape: 'step 14 calls simulation.step(N) with N chosen so population >= 8 000; measure N once and record it in docs/builds/democity_r<n>.json. If the pre-roll pushes stageMs past 20 s, cut ticks before cutting city — and if population is still < 8 000 at 20 s, report the achieved figure in stats() and file it as a simulation tuning finding rather than padding world.economy.'

gaps.property: Rules for role prompts (duplication is a defect: it will drift)
gaps.problem: Section 6's first seven bullets restate BUILDER.md lines 86-91 almost one-for-one (washed-out noon and milky golden hour, night that is dusk, emissive sprites brighter than what they light, per-pixel static from an interpolated varying, obvious tiling, specular sparkle without a roughness floor, z-fighting, floating/sunk objects). Item 21's `grep -rn "Math.random"` restates CRITIC.md line 46. Section 8's 'the dev server belongs to the orchestrator and is never started, stopped or restarted' restates BUILDER.md lines 32-33. Section 4's 'an impression with no file and no probe row behind it is not a finding' restates CRITIC.md's Evidence section. The democity-specific bullets in section 6 (grid-not-a-city, density spread over the map, camera drift, staging outliving setup, init timeout, duplicated ornament, cross-module writes) are the ones that earn their place; the rest will drift the day BUILDER.md is edited.
gaps.fix: Open section 6 with 'BUILDER.md's failure-mode list applies unchanged; the citations below are the rounds where each one landed in a neighbour, and the bullets after them are democity-only', then keep one line per generic trap carrying only the critic-report reference and the democity-specific consequence, and delete the restated advice. Drop the Math.random grep from item 21 (CRITIC.md already runs it) and the dev-server sentence from section 8.

gaps.property: Property 3 (numeric) — a small arithmetic muddle in the weighting scheme
gaps.problem: Item 22 is tagged [minor] but contains a clause graded as a blocker. The weighting block says 'Minors are recorded with evidence and cost at most 0.2 in total' while also saying item 22's must-not-auto-start clause caps the score at 6. A critic scoring a run where the tour auto-starts has to reconcile a 0.2-cost minor with a hard cap in the same item.
gaps.fix: Split it into two items: '22. [blocker] The camera never moves during a capture' (the headless / speed === 0 / camera= probe, Δ < 0.01 m after 3 s, tourState().running === false) and '23. [minor] Camera tour exists' (>= 8 named stops, hours, 4-10 s dwell, flyTo, democity:tour, loop, gotoStop). Renumber and update the blocker/major/minor lists.

strengths: Measurement conventions are defined once, in one place, and every item names which scale it uses (480-px whole frame vs full resolution) — luminance formula, BRIGHT CLUSTERS (L>150, 8-connected, >=4 px), AUTOCORRELATION (detrend by 101-px moving average, max |r| over lags 24-400 <= 0.55), FLAT-PATCH (24x24 windows at stride 12, std < 6, fail at >=5% of frame), ROAD REGION by single-session group-visibility diff. This removes the usual builder/critic argument surface entirely for items 3, 4, 5, 17, 18.

The shot set is closed and self-consistent: 37 PNGs across blocks (a)-(f), and the claim 'every file any acceptance item names appears here' actually holds — I checked all 24 items against the list and found no orphan filename and no unused shot. gauntlet.mjs's output naming (`${cam}_${String(t).replace('.','p')}.png`, dir `shots/<mod>/r<round>`) matches the spec's `<dir>` and `r<n>s7` conventions exactly, and --seed/--times/--timeout all exist as used.

Line-level dependency citations are real, not decorative. Verified: registry.js:12 group creation, :15 apis assignment, :36 `modules: this.apis`, :99 get(name), the 30 s init timeout; camera.js:123 screenToGround, :10 fov 45, and every quoted preset (aerial pitch 0.85 d520, skyline yaw 2.2 pitch 0.16 d900 target [0,40,0], street d60 [40,0,40], closeup d110 [20,6,20], overview :24, night_street :28); props/index.js:234-249 api with no place(), :190 roads:changed listener, :199 the 0.12 s settle; world.js:96 services kinds verbatim, :100-101 placeholders, :105 world.transit; economy.js:413-414/420 coverage vocabulary; screenshot.mjs:101 cameraState. The shot JSON really does carry moduleMs, heapMB, textures, modules.<name>.initMs.

Known failure modes are sourced from this project's own critic reports, and the citations check out — roads_r1 #1/#3 (floating/sunk, bridge decks), #4 (washed-out noon), #5 (specular sparkle); environment_r1 #2/#3; environment_r2 #1/#2 (per-pixel static from an interpolated varying) and #12, whose detail really does record four captures lost to another agent's mid-run save; effects_r1 #1/#2; simulation_r1 #1/#2; terrain_r1 #8; ui_r1 #5 (night-lit backdrop). Plus five democity-specific traps (grid-not-a-city, density spread over the whole map, camera drift, staging outliving setup, init timeout) that no role file carries.

The weighting scheme is complete and internally consistent (12 blockers + 11 majors + 1 minor; every per-item tag matches the summary list), and it is explicitly a ceiling, never a floor — 'a checklist fully met that still reads as section 3's 7 scores 7' closes the usual loophole where a builder satisfies the list and produces something ugly.

The attribution rule (inherited vs composition defect) is settled in advance with a mechanical test — does it reproduce in that module's own showcase at the same camera and hour — which is exactly what a showcase that boots all 16 modules needs.

Budget is consistent with ARCHITECTURE section 9 and with constants.js (perModuleDrawCalls.democity = 50 verified), the 220/900k declared budget is flagged as an assumption rather than smuggled in, and every budget row names the file and key it is read from.

The 16-step staging pipeline in section 8 makes the hard ordering constraints explicit (all assets requested before any await; roads.rebuild once; zoning.bulk once; spawn -> setLevel -> flush; hookScene after staging), so two builders would produce the same sequence — and it correctly explains why each order matters (25 s ceiling, assets.settle(20000) console error).
verdict:
8.0 — fail (pass is 8.5), but a near miss with a short fix list. This is the strongest module spec in the repo on the axes the standard weights hardest: the measurement conventions are defined once and referenced by name, the 37-shot set closes exactly over the 24 acceptance items with no orphan file, the weighting scheme is complete and is explicitly a ceiling rather than a floor, the failure modes are real citations from this project's critic reports (I verified roads_r1 #1/#3/#4/#5, environment_r1 #2/#3, environment_r2 #1/#2/#12, effects_r1 #1/#2, simulation_r1 #1/#2, terrain_r1 #8, ui_r1 #5 — including environment_r2 #12's four lost captures), and the budget matches ARCHITECTURE §9 and constants.js with the one deviation stated as an assumption rather than smuggled in. Nearly every line-level API citation is exact.

It fails on Lens 1. Four places force a builder to guess, and one of them is a blocker they cannot satisfy: item 7's grade-separated ramp needs Δy ≥ 5.5 m, but roads derives every node height from terrain (build.js:470-481), sets designY at addNode and never lets a caller change it, and overwrites opts.elevation at build.js:499 — so there is no public lever, and item 21 re-grades it at seed 7 where terrain luck will not repeat. Items 10 and 12 (two majors, plus §8's required contents) grade democity on park trees, park lamps, crown-colour variety and suburban street-tree spacing that item 15 forbids it to place because props is real, with no statement of the indirect lever (props scatters forest where there is no road and no lot) and no probe naming where the counts are read. §7 merges `world.zones` with `ctx.modules.zoning` into one list, so the single most important call in the pipeline — `bulk(fn)` — reads as available on an object that does not have it, and §8's own catch-all would turn that throw into a silently empty city. And §7 states traffic is a stub when it is a complete module with routing, IDM and pedestrians, which also invalidates §5's stated rationale for the 220-draw-call budget.

It also fails Lens 2, less severely: about six of 24 items carry a clause I could not check mechanically — roof colours and house silhouettes counted by eye, an undefined 'block' in item 11, 'or an equivalent silhouette', 'distinguishable' lit sources, 'a lit downtown canyon, not a suburban street'. Three of those sit inside blockers, which is where an argument costs the most.

Fix the four Lens-1 items and give the six eyeball clauses probe rows and this is a 9. As it stands it would cost the first round to the ramp and the second to the ornament ownership question, which is exactly what this spec exists to prevent.
